title: Nimos (or Avnimos) the Weaver
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: A great philosopher among the sages of the nations of the world in the time of R' Meir. In Chagigah 15b he asked R' Meir: Does all wool that goes down into the cauldron come up? etc.

And in Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 2, section 13 [supplied בב״ר פ״ב־יג; compare Ruth Rabbah 2:13]: Avnimos HaGardi's mother died, and Rabbi Meir went up to show him his face (to pay a condolence visit), and found them sitting as mourners. After a time his father died, and Rabbi Meir found them occupied in their work. He said to him: It seems to me that your mother is dearer to you than your father. He said to him: Is it not written, ‘a woman to her mother’s house’? He said to him: You have spoken well, for you have no father.

And in Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 65, section 2 [supplied פס״ה־ב; compare the saying at 65:20], and in the Petichta of Eichah Rabbah, section 2: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: No philosophers have arisen in the world like Balaam son of Beor and like Avnimos HaGardi. And in Shemot Rabbah, beginning of chapter 13: He asked our Sages, of blessed memory: How was the earth created at first? They said to him: Go to Abba Yosef the builder, etc.

notes.text: The concluding creation question is abbreviated to a direction to Abba Yosef the builder, etc.; its respondent is not named in this notice. The printed midrash divisions are retained.

Nimos and Avnimos remain the supplied alternative names; HaGardi is rendered the Weaver without an identity merge. The p002 personal abbreviation ר״מ is kept as R' Meir at both occurrences; the inherited short Chagigah quotation is not a newly bound whole named scalar. The supplied mourning locator בב״ר פ״ב־יג is retained as Bereshit Rabbah chapter 2 section 13, beside the whole saved Torat Emet digital match at Ruth Rabbah 2:13; the old failed Bereshit Rabbah request remains a failure and does not prove a misprint or correction history. The Ruth scalar explicitly names Rabbi Meir in this narrative, supporting the two full titles locally. Hyman has singular he-went-up-to-show-him-his-face and then plural mourners/workers, and his concluding you-have-no-father is second person. The named Ruth text instead says a gentile-has-no-father; Hyman's wording is retained as an attributed quotation, not adopted as a statement about actual parentage. Its longer not-to-her-father's-house wording is not imported. Hyman's supplied Bereshit Rabbah chapter 65 section 2 remains beside the whole saved TE 65:20 saying, whose explicit Rabbi Abba bar Kahana supports that local title only; no comparison proves a printed numeral error. Eichah Rabbah Petichta 2 remains unverified. Shemot Rabbah beginning of chapter 13 retains Hyman's unnamed he-asked and our-Sages-of-blessed-memory; the whole saved TE 13:1 names Avnimos and has the Sages reply in the plural, supporting They said to him without inventing an individual respondent. The omitted legal, narrative and creation continuations are not imported beyond etc. The old current note and every historical note remain, and both p003/p004 source holds are retained.

The consulted scan of Hyman, volume III, printed p. 946, gives Ruth Rabbah (רו״ר) 2:13 for the mourning episode and Bereshit Rabbah 65:20 for the philosophers saying, whereas the supplied transcription retained here gives Bereshit Rabbah 2:13 and 65:2. The whole consulted Ruth passage contains the mourning and work contrast but ends with “a gentile has no father”; Hyman’s supplied and printed second-person “you have no father” remains an attributed quotation, not a claim about actual parentage. The whole newly consulted Eichah Rabbah, Petichta 2, explicitly contains Rabbi Abba bar Kahana’s philosophers saying, recovering the other parallel previously left unverified. Davidson Chagigah 15b directly names Nimos asking Rabbi Meir the wool-and-cauldron question; its explanatory continuation is not imported into Hyman’s etc. The whole Shemot Rabbah 13:1 passage explicitly names Avnimos as questioner and has the Sages reply in the plural before directing him to Abba Yosef the builder. The supplied unnamed questioner and abbreviated builder episode remain; neither the alternative names nor the philosophical narratives establish a new authority identity. The earlier notes describe the supplied transcription and the state before these additional inspections.
